dialogues.speaker: Boileau
dialogues.text: If we counted all the cases that occurred as "theater" as well... Most of the stories here don't have happy endings.

dialogues.speaker: Boileau
dialogues.text: Precisely. And where there's a case, there will be victims. It really is very sad.

dialogues.speaker: Boileau
dialogues.text: Even if the culprit was sent to serve time, I'm not sure the tale could be said to have a "happy ending."

dialogues.speaker: Boileau
dialogues.text: I've spent a lot of time at the theater on account of my love for tragic stories, and I've always found myself quite accepting of trials or performances that have tragic endings.

dialogues.speaker: Boileau
dialogues.text: Over time, it's become less and less clear to me — am I sad on account of real compatriots of mine? Or on account of the story?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Do not treat cases like child's play.

dialogues.speaker: Boileau
dialogues.text: They say Fontaine is the Nation of Justice. But I don't think such a reputation can be based solely on our Archon.

dialogues.speaker: Boileau
dialogues.text: Fontainians must have their own justice in their hearts.
